competencies.text: Discuss properties of light waves in communications, navigation, medicine, and entertainment.
Identify innovations such as soundproofing, amplifiers, LEDs, holograms, and lasers.

days.title: Nature of Light Waves
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe the wave nature of light, explain reflection, refraction, and the electromagnetic spectrum, and identify how light is used in communication, navigation, medicine, and entertainment.

💡 What Is Light?

Light is a form of electromagnetic radiation — energy that travels through space as a wave. Unlike sound, light can travel through a vacuum (that's how sunlight reaches Earth).

Light travels at 300,000,000 m/s (3 × 10⁸ m/s) in a vacuum — the fastest speed possible in the universe.

🌊 Wave Properties of Light

PropertyDescriptionExample
Wavelength (λ)Distance between two peaks of a waveRed light = ~700 nm; violet light = ~400 nm
Frequency (f)Number of waves passing a point per secondMeasured in Hertz (Hz)
Speed (c)3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuumSlower in water and glass
AmplitudeHeight of the waveDetermines brightness

c = f × λ (speed = frequency × wavelength)

🪞 Reflection

When light bounces off a surface, we call it reflection. The Law of Reflection says: angle of incidence = angle of reflection.

  • Regular reflection: Smooth surface (mirror) → clear image.
  • Diffuse reflection: Rough surface (wall, paper) → scattered light, no image.

Real-life: Mirrors, periscopes, rear-view mirrors, reflectors on bicycles.

🔍 Refraction

When light passes from one medium to another (e.g., air to water), it bends. This is refraction. It happens because light travels at different speeds in different materials.

  • A straw in a glass of water looks bent.
  • A pool looks shallower than it really is.
  • Eyeglasses and contact lenses correct vision using refraction.
  • Lenses in cameras, microscopes, and telescopes all use refraction.

🌈 The Electromagnetic Spectrum

Light is only the visible part of a larger family of waves called the electromagnetic (EM) spectrum:

TypeUse
Radio wavesAM/FM radio, TV, WiFi, cell signals
MicrowavesCooking, radar, satellite communication
Infrared (IR)TV remotes, thermal imaging, night vision
Visible lightWhat our eyes detect (ROYGBIV)
Ultraviolet (UV)Vitamin D production, sterilization, sunburn
X-raysMedical imaging, airport security
Gamma raysCancer treatment, nuclear reactions

🌍 Light in Everyday Life

  • Communications: Fiber-optic cables carry internet and phone signals using light.
  • Navigation: GPS uses radio waves; lighthouses use visible light.
  • Medicine: X-rays, laser surgery, endoscopes.
  • Entertainment: TVs, LED screens, laser light shows, projectors.

🔬 Modern Light Innovations

  • LEDs: Energy-efficient bulbs (last 25× longer than incandescent).
  • Lasers: Focused beams for surgery, cutting metal, reading barcodes.
  • Holograms: 3D images created by interfering light beams.
  • Fiber optics: Data transmission at the speed of light.

📌 Quick Check

  • Why does a straw look bent in water? (Answer: refraction)
  • Why can't we see UV light? (Answer: our eyes only detect 400–700 nm wavelengths)
  • What kind of wave is used in WiFi? (Answer: radio waves)

days.title: Match Game — Light Innovations
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each light concept or technology to its correct description or example. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: A straw appearing bent in a glass of water
Wavelengths from 400 nm to 700 nm that our eyes detect
TV remote signals and thermal imaging
Medical imaging of bones and airport security
Energy-efficient light bulb lasting 25× longer than incandescent
Focused beam used for surgery and barcode scanning
Data transmission using light through thin glass strands

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Light in Daily Life
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🪞 You look into a mirror and see yourself clearly. What type of reflection is happening?
🥤 A straw looks bent when placed in a glass of water. Which phenomenon explains this?
📱 Your TV remote control works even when pointing at the wall (which reflects signals back to the TV). Which type of EM wave does the remote use?
🏥 A hospital uses a machine that produces images of bones without surgery. Which EM wave is used?
⚡ Your barangay is switching to more energy-efficient streetlights. Which lighting technology is BEST for this purpose?

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Optics Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Optics Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
Which property of light determines its color?
Which EM wave has the SHORTEST wavelength?
The Law of Reflection states that:

choices.label: A) Angle of incidence = angle of reflection
B) Angle of incidence = 2 × angle of reflection
D) Angle of incidence = angle of refraction

escape.text: Which technology uses light to transmit internet data at very high speeds?
Why are sunglasses with UV protection important?

choices.label: A) They block visible light only.
B) They protect eyes from harmful ultraviolet radiation that can damage the cornea.
C) They make things look brighter.
D) They reduce the speed of light.
